items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: And so George Avakian actually, he sued me and the group for royalties and, you know, for commissions.

ctx.x: And so George came over, and I just said, well, you know, forget it. So anyway that -- so anyway we came -- I took over the thing like this, although Layman Engel got the credit for it. The musical director, I was the musical director, and I set up the whole thing. And we came back to New York and went into the Barrymore Theater. This was there -- was there two years.

And so George Avakian actually, he sued me and the group for royalties and, you know, for commissions. And I got a lawyer, and we went to court, and they just laughed it out of court because they knew that, you know, I'd been into this jazz for 50 some years, and here's a guy that's just, you know, coming into it from reading books. And -- and he had no -- didn't have any grounds to stand on as far as that is concerned, see, because they -- he actually took the show away from me in the beginning. I could have…
So anyway, we stayed -- was over there two years, and during that period we was there, well, Marlon Brando was --
